description: A Raspberry Pi 4 Model B or Raspberry Pi 5 single-board computer with a 40-pin GPIO header, modelled as a Python API.
summary: The board runs the user's program in the iynk interpreter, in Python with gpiozero. It is a Python API model, not Raspberry Pi OS. Pins, PWM, I2C and timing follow the pi4-pi5 board profile.
ideeprom: Reserved for the HAT identification EEPROM. Leave it alone.

models.1: Python subset run by the interpreter with the Raspberry Pi BCM pin numbers (GPIO17 is physical pin 11).
models.2: Digital I/O, PWM and edge callbacks on GPIO0 to GPIO27 through gpiozero, and RPi.GPIO on the Pi 4.
models.3: I2C master on GPIO2 and GPIO3 and serial output. The Pi 4 and the Pi 5 differ only in clock speed.

not.1: Linux, the desktop and Raspberry Pi OS: this is a Python API model, not an operating system.
not.2: The camera, display, network, USB and PCI Express stacks.
not.3: Analog inputs: the board has none, so an ADC chip such as the MCP3008 is needed.

gap: No electrical ratings are listed yet, so no pin-overload check exists for this board.
